solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Can these exercises hurt? Ultimately, yes

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: things commonly sold in cans

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A gym-goer wonders whether these workouts will be painful, and the answer comes back yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can these' looks like the start of a question but is the definition: tinned fruit you might buy in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaches are among the most familiar tinned fruits, so they are things one might can.

clue.text: Trial of one involved in conspiracy

indicators.note: something involved in a thing sits within it, so it goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone implicated in a conspiracy is put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks legal, but it is an experimental test run.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme is a trial run, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Naked and bearing gold, King Cole violated rule

indicators.note: in a down clue, bearing something means carrying it on top, so it comes first
a rule violated is broken, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Nat King Cole, the American singer

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme king, nude and wearing gold, broke the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole suggests the nursery rhyme, but it is the singer Nat King Cole.
explanation.definitionFit: Au naturel is a French phrase used in English to mean nude, in a natural state.

clue.text: Gathering mist gathered on top

indicators.note: gathered here means drawn in tighter, so the word is shortened by a letter

blocks.note: haar is a cold sea mist on Britain's east coast

explanation.surface: A mist rolls in and settles over the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: haar loses one of its A's to give HAR. 'On top' also places that mist first.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the gathering in of a crop, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Son put on uniform that's considered lucky

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above, so this letter comes first

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy dons a lucky uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing, but here it is the adjective meaning regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is traditionally regarded as a lucky number, so it is a number considered lucky.

clue.text: Six hundred promissory notes? That's brutal!

blocks.note: IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Someone is outraged at being handed six hundred debt notes instead of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicious and brutal are synonyms, both describing savage cruelty.

clue.text: Spinal Tap interminably playing with reverb at the end of dial

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off
the end means only the last letter of the following word
playing suggests the letters being played about with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: The spoof rock band Spinal Tap plays endlessly with the reverb knob turned up full.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinal Tap is the mock heavy-metal band whose amplifiers go up to eleven; the band name splits so 'Spinal' becomes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebral means relating to the vertebrae, the bones of the spine, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Start to cultivate relations with one meditative resident

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: it is a euphemism for sexual relations
Zen is the meditative school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to build friendships with a calm, contemplative local.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen is an inhabitant of a town or country, so a resident.

clue.text: Hope he got rid of spasm of the eye

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so those letters are taken out of the first word

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary muscular spasm

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a man has shaken off a twitch in his eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to the eye or vision.

clue.text: Following Euros' final, Harry Kane scrutinises crap score

indicators.note: final points to the last letter only of the word before it
to harry is to harass and disturb, so the letters are knocked out of order
following means coming after, so this letter leads the rest

blocks.note: to eye is to look over closely

explanation.surface: After the Euro final, England striker Harry Kane studies his poor match statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Kane is the England football captain, but 'Harry' is the anagram signal. Crap is the dice game craps, not a slang insult.
explanation.definitionFit: In craps, a throw of two ones is called snake eyes, the lowest possible score.

clue.text: Both sides on vehicle

blocks.note: left and right, L AND R
on top of, as in over

explanation.surface: Something is fitted on each side of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Both sides are left and right, written L AND R with the word 'and' kept whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A Land Rover is a make of off-road car, an example of a vehicle.

clue.text: White tray containing fish

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, so it is found within their run of letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A white serving tray holds a fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: The Three Amigos say 'time to wear hat'

indicators.note: a hat that something must wear goes around it, so the hat word encloses the other

blocks.note: tile is slang for a hat
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone imitates the comedy trio announcing it is time to put on hats, sombreros perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old British slang for a hat. 'Say' marks the film name as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Three Amigos! is the name of a 1986 comedy film, so it is an example of a title.

clue.text: Creator of Superman zine mingling with the leaders of science-fiction comics

indicators.note: things mingling get mixed together, so all these letters are jumbled
leaders come at the front, so each following word gives its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of science-fiction and comics

explanation.surface: A fanzine about the comic-book hero is mixed in with leading sci-fi comics.
explanation.walkthrough: Superman suggests the DC hero, but the philosopher's Übermensch is usually translated Superman; 'the' joins the fodder as well as appearing to introduce leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche introduced the idea of the Übermensch, rendered in English as the Superman.

clue.text: Carry one who's lying, or who's just got up?

blocks.note: first meaning: a frame for carrying a patient lying down; also one who is lying, stretching the truth
second meaning: someone just out of bed who stretches their limbs

explanation.walkthrough: 'One who's lying' does double duty: a patient lying flat, and a teller of tall tales who stretches the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a carrying frame for the injured, an exaggerator, and anyone stretching after waking.

clue.text: Sweet treat from Cornwall, perhaps, is second on list

blocks.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, SW
S is the abbreviation for second
a roll is a list of names; on places it last

explanation.surface: A Cornish pudding comes in at number two in a ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a rolled sponge cake with jam filling, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Money invested in topiary, whimsically, by duke

blocks.note: D for duke, placed by the rest

explanation.surface: An aristocrat has put money into fanciful garden sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge fund is a pooled investment fund, money invested on behalf of clients.

clue.text: Get out of town and head to Russia, leaving country

indicators.note: a head is the front of something, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped from the country

blocks.note: the head, or first letter, of Russia

explanation.surface: A traveller flees town for Russia, quitting their own country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out of town' reads as an instruction to travel, but it is the exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal exclamations of disbelief, so the phrases are idiomatic equivalents.

clue.text: Dress or gown with red hood?

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or put in order, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Choosing between a dress and a gown, with Little Red Riding Hood in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like a garment beside dress and gown, but it is short for hoodlum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood is a hoodlum, a gangster, so a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Solomon had managed to get wasted

blocks.note: the setter Solomon speaking: I'd, meaning I had

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of having contrived to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for I or me. 'Wasted' suggests drunk but means spent time doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idled means let time pass doing nothing, which is wasting time.

clue.text: He gives a moving performance and cycles Parisian streets backwards

indicators.note: cycles means rotates, so the last letter moves round to the front
backwards means the word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: A performer gives a touching show and pedals backwards through the streets of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving performance' suggests emotion, but it is literal: a dancer moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, someone who performs through movement.

clue.text: Tasty coulis I'd blended with the end of pestle

indicators.note: ingredients blended are mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the end means the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A cook describes a fruit sauce ground with a pestle.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicious and tasty are synonyms for food with a pleasing flavour.

clue.text: Cold mountainous region in the north- west?

definitions.text: Cold mountainous region in the north- west?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A chilly, hilly area in the north-west of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a cold, mountainous county in north-west England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is the English county containing the Lake District fells, in the far north-west.

clue.text: Tiger seen jumping into lion's territory?

indicators.note: letters jumping about land in a different order

explanation.surface: A tiger is spotted leaping into ground belonging to a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the Tanzanian plain famous for its lion prides; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: Revive Frenchman with whiskey

blocks.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A French man is brought round with a glass of whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restore or refresh, which matches revive.

clue.text: Home help returning in a state

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A domestic helper comes back in an agitated condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as flustered, but state here means a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a sovereign nation, which is one sense of a state.

clue.text: Charming old lady rolling small cigarette

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the following word is read backwards

blocks.note: an old lady is a mother, ma
cig is the short form of cigarette

explanation.surface: A delightful elderly woman rolls herself a little smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic as an adjective means enchanting or wonderful, the same as charming.

clue.text: Off-white top

blocks.note: first meaning: a pale yellowish-white colour
second meaning: the best part, as in the pick of the bunch

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a garment description; both words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pale colour and, figuratively, the best of something, since it rises to the top of milk.

clue.text: Jump topless for a little bit

indicators.note: without a top, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to jump on something is to pounce

explanation.surface: Someone leaps around half-naked for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small weight, so figuratively a tiny amount.

clue.text: Where lexicographer might put doner kebab that's not ready

definitions.text: Where lexicographer might put doner kebab

blocks.clueFragment: Where lexicographer might put doner kebab
blocks.note: first meaning: in a dictionary, doner follows, so sits beneath, the word done

explanation.walkthrough: Dictionary entries are alphabetical, so doner kebab is listed just below the headword DONE: under DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Underdone food is undercooked, not yet ready to eat.

clue.text: Cowboy could become depressed after breaking up

indicators.note: splitting the first word into two parts lets each half be read on its own

blocks.note: the whole word, which is broken into its two halves below
a cow lows, so it is a lower

explanation.surface: A cowhand might get gloomy after a romance ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowboy' must be split: a cow is something that lows, and Ed is a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowered means brought down, as spirits or mood are when depressed.

clue.text: Characters shaken, hit by a horse

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: a, plus nag for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone is rattled after being struck by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: the answer is the very device the solver deals with constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a word made by rearranging letters, so its characters have been shaken up.
